theme: Blessed is the man who fears the LORD
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 112. It is the companion to Psalm 111. Where Psalm 111 described the LORD, this psalm describes the person who fears the LORD, and the person turns out to be like him. Paul quotes verse 9 in 2 Corinthians 9:9.
settingTheScene: Psalm 112 is also an acrostic, with twenty-two short lines. It describes the blessed person who fears the LORD and delights in his commandments. The pairing with Psalm 111 is intentional: many phrases are repeated, like “his righteousness endures forever.” What is said of God is also said of the godly person. This is the Bible’s picture of becoming like the one we worship. It also anticipates Paul’s teaching about generosity at the end of the unit.
observation: “Praise the LORD! Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in his commandments!” (v. 1).
“Light dawns in the darkness for the upright; he is gracious, merciful, and righteous” (v. 4).
“It is well with the man who deals generously and lends; who conducts his affairs with justice” (v. 5).
“For the righteous will never be moved; he will be remembered forever” (v. 6).
“He is not afraid of bad news; his heart is firm, trusting in the LORD” (v. 7).
“His heart is steady; he will not be afraid” (v. 8).
“He has distributed freely; he has given to the poor” (v. 9).
“His righteousness endures forever; his horn is exalted in honor” (v. 9).
interpretation:
The psalm opens with a beatitude: “Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in his commandments!” Fear and delight go together. The fear of the LORD is not terror but reverence, and obedience is a joy, not a burden. The blessing extends to the next generation: “His offspring will be mighty in the land.” Wealth and righteousness are mentioned, but the focus is on the character that lasts: “his righteousness endures forever.” This is the same phrase used of God in Psalm 111:3. The godly person reflects the character of God.

Verse 4 gives the surprising line: “Light dawns in the darkness for the upright; he is gracious, merciful, and righteous.” Again, the words “gracious and merciful” are used of God in Psalm 111:4. The person who fears the LORD is a light for others in dark times, and he receives light himself. Then comes generosity: “It is well with the man who deals generously and lends; who conducts his affairs with justice.” Faith expresses itself in the use of money and in fairness.

Verse 6 says “The righteous will never be moved; he will be remembered forever.” This echoes the stability of the one who trusts in the LORD. Verse 7: “He is not afraid of bad news; his heart is firm, trusting in the LORD.” How many of us live in fear of bad news? The believer’s security rests on a faithful God, not on good circumstances. This does not mean no bad news will come, but that it cannot shake us. “His heart is steady; he will not be afraid, until he looks in triumph on his adversaries.”

Verse 9 is the center: “He has distributed freely; he has given to the poor; his righteousness endures forever; his horn is exalted in honor.” Paul quotes this verse in 2 Corinthians 9:9 to encourage the Corinthians to give to the poor believers in Jerusalem. Generosity is a sign of righteousness. And God, who supplies seed to the sower, will multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.

The psalm ends with a contrast: “The wicked man sees it and is angry; he gnashes his teeth and melts away; the desire of the wicked will perish!” Those who reject God’s ways cannot stand the light of the righteous. But the one who fears the LORD will not be shaken.

In the end, the one who perfectly fits this psalm is Christ, who feared the LORD, delighted in his commands, gave freely to the poor, and has been exalted in honor. We are being made like him.
connection: 2 Corinthians 9:6-15 quotes verse 9 in the context of giving. Psalm 111 is the companion. Psalm 1 also describes the blessed man. Proverbs 19:17 says whoever is generous to the poor lends to the LORD. Matthew 5:14-16 calls us the light of the world. Luke 6:35-36 says be merciful as your Father is merciful. Ephesians 5:1 says be imitators of God. 1 Timothy 6:17-19 commands the rich to be generous. Isaiah 26:3 speaks of perfect peace for those whose mind is stayed on the LORD.
application:
Ask where bad news makes you afraid. Pray verse 7 and give that worry to God.

Give something to someone in need this week, quietly. Do it with the attitude of verse 9.

Notice where your character looks like the character of God. Thank him. Notice where it doesn’t. Ask him to change it.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to make you gracious, merciful, and righteous.
Tell him you want to fear him and delight in his commandments.
Ask him to give you generosity.
